question: Solve $3x+y=11$ and $2x+y=7$ by using the inverse of the coefficient matrix. Hence, calculate $x^2+y^2$.
explanation:
Formation of the matrix equation
The system is represented by $$\begin{bmatrix}3&1\\2&1\end{bmatrix}\begin{bmatrix}x\\y\end{bmatrix}=\begin{bmatrix}11\\7\end{bmatrix}$$
Inverse of the coefficient matrix
The determinant is $(3)(1)-(1)(2)=1$. Hence, $$A^{-1}=\begin{bmatrix}1&-1\\-2&3\end{bmatrix}$$
Determination of $x$ and $y$
Therefore, $$X=A^{-1}B=\begin{bmatrix}1&-1\\-2&3\end{bmatrix}\begin{bmatrix}11\\7\end{bmatrix}=\begin{bmatrix}4\\-1\end{bmatrix}$$ Thus, $x=4$ and $y=-1$.
Evaluation of the expression
Hence, $$x^2+y^2=4^2+(-1)^2=17$$
